name: Miranda warnings
source: Part II 6.1: Miranda warnings (1966) are in force; a suspect may refuse to talk and may have a lawyer. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: Title III wiretap
source: Part II 6.3: the federal wiretap statute (Title III, 1968) permits eavesdropping only on a judge's order, for a limited set of serious crimes, for 30 days (renewable), with a duty to minimize; Justice Department sign-off first. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: New Jersey one-party consent recording
source: Part II 6.3: New Jersey's wiretap act (1968) allows recording with the consent of one party (N.J.S.A. 2A:156A-4). The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: informant body wire
source: Part II 6.3: an informant may carry a transmitter or recorder and agents may testify to what they hear, without a warrant (United States v. White, decided 5 April 1971, six to three).

name: pen register
source: Part II 6.3: a pen register needs no warrant after Smith v. Maryland (June 1979); before then its status is murkier (so it exists, status unsettled, at the 1975 baseline: the bible gives no earlier date). Part II 9: 1979, 'fixed after'. The bible gives the month only; the last day of the month is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: grand jury civil contempt, 18 months at most
aliases: civil contempt for refusing to testify
source: Part II 6.4: a witness who refuses after immunity can be jailed for civil contempt until he talks, until the grand jury's term ends, or for 18 months at most (28 U.S.C. 1826). The bible gives no enactment date; the rule is in force at the 1 January 1975 baseline.

name: RICO
aliases: Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act
source: Part II 6.6: enacted October 1970 but little used; the first jury conviction under it was United States v. Parness, October 1973 (affirmed 1974). Before the late 1970s prosecutors prefer gambling, extortion, tax evasion, narcotics conspiracy, Hobbs Act, interstate theft, labor racketeering. 'Available' is the first conviction. The bible gives months only; the last day of the month is used.

name: RICO used against organized crime
aliases: RICO begins to be used against organized crime
source: Part II 9 (1978 onward, rising) and Part III 13.2: RICO begins to be used against organized crime. Part II 6.6 Weather: from the late 1970s to 1985 it moves from the law books to the front line. A pressure of rising strength, not an outcome.

name: RICO case against a union leader (United States v. Scotto)
source: Part II 6.6: a RICO case against a New York longshoremen's union leader was brought in the Southern District of New York in September 1979. The real person is offstage only. The bible gives the month only; the last day of the month is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: RICO prosecution of a Mafia leadership
aliases: RICO prosecution of a crime family
source: Part II 6.6 and 9: the first major Mafia leadership case is the Commission case, indicted on 25 February 1985, tried in 1986, verdicts on 19 November 1986. Use against Mafia leadership comes later than the first RICO convictions.

name: Witness Security Program
source: Part II 6.7: WITSEC is authorized in 1970 and begins in 1971, run by the U.S. Marshals; untested in a mob context at scale until the late 1970s. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: Bank Secrecy Act
source: Part I 9.6 and Part III 7.8: since the Bank Secrecy Act of 1970, banks file reports on cash transactions above $10,000; on paper after 1970, few filed. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: Landrum-Griffin Act
source: Part IV 2.3: the 1959 labor-management reporting law requires secret-ballot election of local officers at least every three years and bars certain convicted persons from union office for five years after conviction or release, whichever is later; the bar does not take effect until the conviction is upheld on appeal. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: union-office bar lengthened to thirteen years
aliases: Comprehensive Crime Control Act union bar
source: Part IV 2.3 and 2.9: on 12 October 1984 the Comprehensive Crime Control Act lengthens the bar from five years to thirteen for later convictions, lets a court cut it to no less than three, and makes it take effect at conviction.

name: federal preventive detention
source: Part II 6.2 and 9: before the Bail Reform Act of 1984 federal defendants in non-capital cases had a right to release unless a judge believed they would flee; dangerousness was not a ground for detention, so do not hold a boss without bail on the strength of his reputation. The 1984 act (12 October 1984 per Part IV 2.3) allows detention for dangerousness; the Supreme Court upholds it in 1987.

name: preventive detention upheld by the Supreme Court
source: Part II 6.2 and 9: 'fixed after' 1987. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: forensic DNA profiling
source: Part II 6.8: no DNA testing in 1975; forensic DNA profiling arrives in 1986 and reaches courts from 1987. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: undercover infiltration of a Mafia family
aliases: FBI undercover agent in a family
source: Part II 7.2 and 9: such an operation, if it occurs, begins no earlier than 1976 and is rare and hard; a famous New York case runs September 1976 to July 1981. A possibility from 1976, not an event.

name: FBI Top Echelon Criminal Informant Program
source: Part II 7.1: began in 1961 and ran until 1978, when the Bureau replaced it with a general Criminal Informant Program. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: Attorney General guidelines on informants
source: Part II 7.1 and 9: first Attorney General guidelines on informants, 15 December 1976 (domestic security investigations guidelines 6 April 1976).

name: Church Committee
source: Part II 9: Senate select committee formed January 1975, report April 1976; Bureau cautious about bugs and informants. 'Available' is the report. The bible gives the month only; the last day of the month is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: Parole Commission
source: Part II 8: a Parole Commission reorganized in May 1976 sets release dates by guideline. The bible gives the month only; the last day of the month is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: DEA
source: Part II 5: DEA formed 1 July 1973; works heroin and cocaine cases and is the FBI's rival over drugs.

name: ERISA
source: Part II 5 and Part IV 2.6: signed 2 September 1974 (Public Law 93-406); reporting and disclosure rules and most fiduciary standards take effect 1 January 1975.

name: Abscam
source: Part II 9: a sting begins in March 1978 and becomes public in early February 1980; congressional convictions follow in 1981. 'Available' is the public disclosure. The bible gives the month only; the last day of the month is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: New Jersey death penalty reinstated
source: Part II 8: de facto ban from 1972, reinstated in 1982 (last execution 22 January 1963). The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: New Jersey Lottery
source: Part III 7.2 and Part VI 2.3: created 20 November 1969. A weekly game with long odds that did not compete with the illegal numbers game (Part I 9.8).

name: State daily numbers game (Pick-it)
source: Part I 9.8, 13 and Part VI 2.3, 10: the State's daily three-digit game begins 22 May 1975, first called Pick-it and renamed Pick-3 in 1987; prizes parimutuel. A strong, slow pressure on the numbers banks, not a fixed outcome.

name: Pennsylvania daily number
source: Part VI 10.1: begins 1 March 1977.

name: New Jersey Pick-6
source: Part VI 11.2 (anchors): Pick-6 began 9 May 1980.

name: New York daily number
source: Part VI 10.1: begins 1980; the exact start date is Open. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: Atlantic City casino gambling referendum
source: Part I 13 and Part VI 10.1: New Jersey votes for casinos in November 1976, for Atlantic City only. The bible gives the month only; the last day of the month is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: Atlantic City casino
source: Part I 9.9, 13 and Part VI 10.1: Resorts opens 26 May 1978; Saint Jude gets no casino.

name: Contraband Cigarette Trafficking Act
source: Part VI 10.1: enacted 2 November 1978 (Public Law 95-575), trafficking provision in effect about 1 March 1979.

name: New Jersey income tax
source: Part VI 10.1: passed July 1976, first withholding 3 September 1976. The bible gives the month only; the last day of the month is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: containerization at Port Newark
source: Part I 3.1a: containerization began at Port Newark on 26 April 1956 (the Ideal X).

name: Elizabeth Marine Terminal
source: Part I 3.1a: opened 15 August 1962.

name: Gannet Terminal
source: Part I 2.5 (history table: the container port opens on the South Flats, the Gannet Terminal opens in 1968), tagged Anchor model; second tier next to Newark and Elizabeth. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: State Commission of Investigation
source: Part I 3.1a and Part II 1.1, 4.5: the real New Jersey body, created in 1968, working from 1 January 1969, with subpoena power and public hearings but no power to prosecute.

name: Killbuck Waterfront Commission
source: Part I 2.5 (history table): created by the State in 1954 as a sister to the real bi-state Waterfront Commission of New York Harbor of 1953; registers dock workers. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: Conrail
source: Part I 13: Conrail forms in 1976 (Penn Central bankruptcy 1970). The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: Motor Carrier Act and Staggers Rail Act
source: Part I 13 and Part IV 2.9: deregulate trucking and rail in 1980. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: cellular phone
source: Part I 13: commercial cellular service begins late 1983 [memory]. The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: telephone monopoly breakup
source: Part I 13: the telephone monopoly breaks up (1984). The bible gives the year only; the last day of the year is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: Pizza Connection
source: Part III 13.1 and Part V: arrests April 1984; trial September 1985 to March 1987. 'Available' is the start of the trial. The bible gives the month only; the last day of the month is used so that the rule is never applied early.

name: money laundering statute
source: Part IV 3.7, 7 (Weather) and Part VI 10.1: federal forfeiture, money-laundering and currency-reporting enforcement tightens from 1984 (Part VI: 1984 to 1985; Part IV: 'an act of 1986'). 'Exists' is the start of the tightening, 'available' the year of the act, year only so the last day is used. Both marks are [memory, to verify].

name: crack cocaine
source: Part I 13, Part II 9, Part III 13.1, Part V 9.5, Part VI 10.1: rock cocaine is rare in the Northeast until about 1984; appears 1984 to 1985; the boom is 1985 to 1987. 'Exists' is the start of the appearance window, 'available' the start of the boom. A pressure, not an outcome.

name: car phone
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): Bell System Mobile Telephone Service began in St. Louis in June 1946; the improved IMTS followed in 1964. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: pager
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): Al Gross's hospital pager dates from 1949; Motorola's Pageboy I tone pager from 1964. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: numeric display pager
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): approximate dates. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: fax machine
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): Xerox Long Distance Xerography (1964), Magnafax Telecopier (1966); wide adoption in the mid 1980s. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: videocassette recorder
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): Sony U-matic 1971, Betamax in the US November 1975, VHS 1977; common in the mid 1980s (estimate). Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: video rental store
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): the first rental shops opened in 1977 to 1978 (estimate). Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: answering machine
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): sold from the late 1940s; the consumer Phone-Mate in 1971; 'common' is an estimate. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: answering service
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): a human switchboard service; the dates are loose estimates. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: portable tape recorder
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): the Philips compact cassette appeared in August 1963; 'available' and 'common' are estimates. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: body recorder
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): Nagra recorders date from 1951; agencies used them on informants from the 1960s. The legal side (informant wire without a warrant, 5 April 1971) is in the 'informant body wire' entry. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: closed-circuit camera
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): closed-circuit television exists at specific sites; no citywide network is modelled before 1990. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: personal computer
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): the Altair 8800 was announced in January 1975, the Apple II went on sale in June 1977, the IBM PC in August 1981; 'common' is an estimate. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: office photocopier
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): the Xerox 914 was shown in September 1959; 'common' is an estimate. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: automatic teller machine
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): first cash machine in London in June 1967, first US machines in New York in September 1969; 'common' is an estimate. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: bank credit card
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): BankAmericard launched September 1958, Master Charge association 1966; 'common' is an estimate. Package assumption, real-world dates.

name: compact disc
source: Not from the bible (it has no technology ladder): players on sale in Japan October 1982 and in the US March 1983; 'common' is an estimate. Package assumption, real-world dates.
